title: Thermodynamics: laws, efficiency and blackbody radiation
mission: Curate atomic reusable classical thermodynamics relationships: the first law, engine efficiency, reversible entropy change, blackbody radiation and boundary work, each with explicit reservoir and system scope. Successive batches; no cycle-analysis chain required.
priorities: First-law internal-energy change from heat and work with sign convention explicit
Heat-engine thermal efficiency from work and heat input
Reversible entropy change from heat and absolute temperature
Constant-pressure boundary work from pressure and volume change
boundaries: Carnot COP limits are already covered in the building-energy lane: reference them, do not duplicate them.
Absolute temperature is required wherever temperature enters; reject Celsius inputs used silently as absolute.
Physics vs chemistry sign conventions must be stated per record and used consistently in references.
Exclude statistical-mechanical derivations, non-equilibrium analysis, combustion chemistry (building-energy lane), and equilibrium constants needing exp or log, which must be deferred with sources.
starter_sources: https://openstax.org -- navigate to University Physics Volume 1 chapters on Temperature and Heat and on Thermodynamics; record exact book, edition and section, never cite the root as evidence
Find an engineering thermodynamics textbook (for example Cengel) or equivalent reference for the laws and efficiency records; starter links alone do not prove the equation
special_checks: Guard positive absolute temperature; test zero-heat and zero-work boundaries
Efficiency records must be bounded to [0,1] with stated idealizations
The Stefan-Boltzmann constant enters via constants metadata with source and units; check the T^4 power handling
Sign-convention consistency must hold across expression, guards, references and inverse notes
integration_expectation: Temperature, entropy and heat dimensions are unsupported and require extension. The integer fourth power fits the engine; all seed forms are scalar and validate numerically in the kit. Never relabel temperature as duration or heat as work.
coverage_guidance: Priorities are seeds, not a finite checklist. Continue into adjacent source chapters/subtopics inside the boundaries, selecting independently reusable relationships. Save multiple bounded batches without waiting for owner review. Check supplied inventory and prior returns for equivalent relationships and conflicting IDs. Record out-of-format discoveries as deferred with exact sources and missing capabilities; do not force chains or dilute quality for a quota.
